title: BAPS hosts annual 'Polar Bear Plunge' - NewsBreak
text:
9 hours ago BROKEN ARROW, Okla. — Broken Arrow Public Schools Athletic Department held its annual 'BA Polar Bear Plunge' fundraising event on Wednesday, after poor weather conditions caused the event to be rescheduled.
Athletic teams from across the district, along with the Broken Arrow firefighters and police officers, jumped into cold water to raise money for the district's Special Olympics team.
FOX23 spoke with the head coach of the BA Special Olympics team, Ashley Lemaster, at the fundraiser. She said the team that has the most participants at the event wins a trophy.
"We're going to have a lot of teams come out. Soccer has won the last five years, so we'll see if they get rivaled. We have our cheer, soccer and football. We have some firefighters here and the Jungle Squad, so it's just a really fun day that we get to come out and have fun and have a little bit of rivalry and support our Special Olympics athletes," Lemaster said.
BAPS has been holding the annual event for about 10 years, and all proceeds from the event will help send the district's Special Olympics team to the state games in May.
"We're just very blessed that we have so much support in Broken Arrow. We've gotten to talk to a lot of other schools, and not all the schools and towns are large enough to have the support that we have. So it's just a huge blessing. The more support we have, the more experiences our special needs kids get to have," Lemaster said.
Lemaster described what it's like to see Broken Arrow students rally around the Special Olympics team.
"It's the best feeling just looking and seeing them all and seeing our Special Olympics students go up and say hi to their friends. Our Special Olympics athletes are like rockstars here," Lemaster said.
The event was originally slated for last month, but winter weather caused the event to be postponed until February.
